about: Schematic lower molar in its socket, built in code (src/tooth-model.js). Shapes are simplified for teaching and are not to scale. Each structure uses sources from structures.json.

structures.name: Enamel
structures.summary: The outer layer that covers the dentin of the crown, the part of the tooth that projects above the gum line. Enamel is the hardest substance in the body.
structures.assistant: Hard as it is, enamel can still break down: bacteria feeding on sugars make acids that dissolve its calcium crystals, causing dental caries (cavities).

structures.name: Dentin
structures.summary: A bone-like tissue that surrounds the pulp cavity and makes up most of the tooth. In the crown it is covered by enamel; in the root it is covered by cementum.

structures.name: Pulp cavity (pulp chamber)
structures.summary: The inner space of the tooth. It holds the pulp, a loose connective tissue through which nerves and blood vessels run.

structures.name: Root canal
structures.summary: The part of the pulp cavity that runs through the root of the tooth. Nerves and blood vessels pass through it into the pulp.

structures.name: Cementum
structures.summary: A layer of modified bone that covers the dentin of the root.

structures.name: Periodontal ligament
structures.summary: The connective tissue that holds the root in its socket, between the cementum and the alveolar bone. Its thickness is exaggerated here so it can be seen.

structures.name: Alveolar bone (socket)
structures.summary: The bone of the alveolar process of the mandible or maxilla. Each tooth root sits in a socket (alveolus) in this bone.

structures.name: Gingiva (gums)
structures.summary: Soft tissue that lines the alveolar processes and surrounds the neck of the tooth.
structures.assistant: Bleeding, redness or swelling of the gums is an early sign of gingivitis.
